body:
The changeset you listed shouldn't have modified the internals of the query builder. Are you sure there isn't another changeset that is responsible?

With that said I can take a look into the invalid SQL being generated.

There might be, but that commit is the last time I can see it working. I noticed it doesn't happen if the finder is `all`. If I make it `translations`, it fails. I still can't tell where/what is making it fail. It seems like the join that TranslateBehavior adds is seeing the offset from the main query and keeping it, even though the join shouldn't be using OFFSET or LIMIT.
What does the generated SQL with the invalid syntax look like?

`SELECT i18n.id AS `i18n__id`, i18n.locale AS `i18n__locale`, i18n.model AS `i18n__model`, i18n.foreign_key AS `i18n__foreign_key`, i18n.field AS `i18n__field`, i18n.content AS `i18n__content` FROM i18n AS i18n WHERE (i18n.model = :c0 AND i18n.foreign_key IN (SELECT Articles.id AS `Articles__id` FROM articles AS Articles OFFSET 9))`
heh, this is an issue with the Subselect strategy in the eager loader. It should remove limit and offset entirely
@lorenzo Ok, I can fix up that loading strategy. It should probably also omit `having` and `group`.
@markstory I would be cautious  with removing those 2, they are meaningful in filtering conditions
@lorenzo Ok, I will check if they cause an issue before removing them.
